title: Usage risk matrix & billing handoff worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet is a lightweight, copyable sheet to use during pre-QBR prep and the QBR itself. Focus: quickly triage token spend risk, document recent rate-limit incidents, and produce a clear billing handoff + action list for finance/ENG owners.

How to use:
- Populate the Route-level table with data from billing export + request logs (last 30d + 7d trend).
- Use the Risk Matrix thresholds to color-code (Green/Yellow/Red) customer exposure.
- Capture any outstanding questions and pre-assign owners so the QBR ends with a concrete runbook.

QUICK KPI SNAPSHOT (fill before QBR):
- 30d total tokens: ______
- 7d tokens: ______
- Current month-to-date spend: $______
- Forecast month-end spend (lin. proj): $______
- Tokens/day growth rate (7d -> 1d): ____%
- Active routes: ____  endpoints, ____ models

RISK MATRIX (apply to customer overall and per-route):
- GREEN: stable/expected usage. No alerts in 30d. Forecast <= committed budget.
- YELLOW: 1-2 alerts in 30d OR forecast ~75-95% of budget OR sudden 3-7d growth > 30%.
- RED: >2 alerts or sustained growth >50% in 7d OR forecast >= budget or rate limit > baseline causing errors.

Thresholds (recommended starting points):
- Budget alert: 75% warn, 90% critical, 100% block/notify finance
- Rate-limit saturation: sustained 5% throttling over 30m => Yellow; 20% throttling over 1h => Red
- Unexpected model downgrade failsafe: if fallback invoked >5x/hour => Yellow; >30x/day => Red

ROUTE-LEVEL TOKEN BURN (paste rows for heavy routes)
Columns: route | model | token_type | avg_tokens_per_req | p50_latency_ms | 30d_tokens | 7d_tokens | 24h_tokens | 30d_cost_est | alerts_30d | owner
Example row:
embed-search | text-embed-4 | input | 120 | 85 | 1,200,000 | 300,000 | 48,000 | $960 | 0 | Maya S.

ASCII table template (copy into sheet):
route,model,token_type,avg_tokens_per_req,p50_latency_ms,30d_tokens,7d_tokens,24h_tokens,30d_cost_est,alerts_30d,owner

Known anomalies to check (pre-QBR checklist):
- Sudden spike correlated with marketing event? (yes/no) -> link to campaign ticket
- Batch job started recently (cron/ad-hoc)? -> last deploy timestamp: _____
- Model change or prompt tuning pushed in last 14d? -> PR link
- Any recent client-side retry loop causing amplification? -> review client SDK logs

ALERT TEMPLATES (copy into PagerDuty/Slack/Email):

Slack alert (high severity):
[ALERT] Customer: {{customer_name}} — Token burn spike
30d tokens: {{30d}} | 24h: {{24h}} (+{{24h_pct_change}}%)
Recommended: throttle non-critical routes, enable burst cap fallbacks, notify CS and ENG on-call
Link: {{billing_export_url}}

Email to Finance (budget-critical):
Subject: Urgent: {{customer_name}} projected month spend ${{proj}} — action required
Body: Summary of drivers, recommended credit/overage policy, point of contact (CS owner) and timeline for decision

Playbook: immediate steps when budget crosses thresholds:
1) 75% (notify) — CS sends advisory note + include forecast & recommended mitigations. Open ticket: CS-Alert-{{id}}
2) 90% (escalate) — Finance looped; propose short-term throttle (non-core routes) and apply rate-limit policy. Request approval for overage credit if needed.
3) 100% (block/mitigate) — Apply hard caps if customer consented, or enable slow-fail fallback model. Finance + Legal to sign off on invoice handling.

Billing handoff checklist (what CS gives Finance during QBR):
- Cleaned billing export CSV (30d + MTD)
- Annotated route-level table with explanations for spikes
- List of alerts and timestamps (linked to logs)
- Contractual limits and committed tokens (SLA/plan)
- Proposed shared action: credit request, one-time discount, or revised commit
- Contact info: CS owner, Finance rep, ENG on-call

ENGINEERING ESCALATION (who does what):
- CS owner: initial customer comms, documents product-side mitigations, tracks approvals
- ENG on-call: verifies if throttles or fallback were triggered, applies temporary routing changes if allowed
- Platform/Runtime SME: investigates root cause if throttling >20% or persistent KV cache misses

POST-QBR ACTIONS (assign in meeting):
- Update contract table with revised commit or note credit (owner + ETA)
- Create follow-up engineering ticket: investigate top 2 routes by token delta (link)
- Schedule 2-week check-in to confirm remediation

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF:
- Do we have a standard “soft-throttle” configuration customers accept? (CS to file consent template)
- Clarify whether billing export includes embedding vs generation token split — finance asked last month
- Should we add a per-route anomaly detector (simple z-score) in the console? Proposal ticket: CS-Detect-001

REFERENCES & LINKS (placeholders - fill with real artifacts before QBR):
- Billing export location: /billing/exports/{{customer}}_30d.csv
- Request logs: logs.redwood.internal/{{customer}}/requests?range=30d
- Related Jira: JIRA-CS-4123, JIRA-PLT-879

One-line summary template for QBR slide: 
"Last 30d token growth +54% driven by search-embedding route; projected month spend $X (Y% above plan). Action: enable soft-throttle on non-critical routes, review commit expansion."

Template revision history:
- 2026-02-20 Avery Chen — initial draft
- 2026-03-10 Maya Singh — added alert templates and handoff checklist

Quick copy checklist (for CS owner before QBR):
- [ ] Paste 30d/7d/24h numbers into top KPIs
- [ ] Color-code risk matrix and mark red/yellow/green
- [ ] Export and attach detailed billing CSV to QBR doc
- [ ] Assign follow-ups with owners and due dates

End of worksheet.
